description: MUMmer 3.23 show-snps: the single-base substitutions and indels of every alignment of a nucmer delta file: [P1] reference position, [SUB] the two characters ('.' = indel), [P2] query position, [BUFF] the distance to the nearest other difference in the same alignment, [DIST] the distance to the nearest sequence end, [R] [Q] the number of other alignments over the position (showConflict = false is -C: only unambiguous SNPs and no [R] [Q] columns), optional sequence lengths (-l), context (-x characters each side), frames and ids; a difference between compatible IUPAC codes (N, R/A ...) is not a SNP (the program's asymmetric CompareIUPAC table). sortByReference (-r, default) / sortByQuery (-q), tabular (-T), header = false (-H), showIndels = false (-I), alignments (-S): only the alignments of these show-coords lines. A promer delta file reports the amino-acid substitutions of the translated frames (positions of the nucleotide strand, the context is cut at the end of a translated frame like the program's c_str ()). Byte for byte equal to the installed show-snps on 450 nucmer and 375 + promer runs.

referenceFasta.description: Reference FASTA text (the file named in the delta header).

queryFasta.description: Query FASTA text (the file named in the delta header).

showConflict.description: Report SNPs of ambiguous alignments and show the [R] [Q] columns (default true; false = -C).

sortByQuery.description: -q: sort by query ids and positions (default false; -r wins when both are set).

sortByReference.description: -r: sort by reference ids and positions (the default when neither is set).

context.description: -x: characters of SNP context on each side (default 0).

alignments.description: -S: report only the alignments of these show-coords lines (null = all).

text.description: What show-snps writes to standard output.

messages.description: What it writes to standard error (warnings).

errors.message: Delta file text cannot be null or empty
ERROR: SNP context must be a positive int

examples.name: Three substitutions with two bases of context
